assessment.nobel_worthiness: Random-coefficients demand estimation with endogenous prices (BLP) and the dynamic-industry framework (Ericson-Pakes) changed how demand, market power, mergers and welfare are measured. The methods are used routinely in empirical IO, trade, health and antitrust, and they link rigorous econometrics to policy-relevant counterfactuals.
assessment.attribution: The BLP contribution is cleanly attributable to Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes. Pakes also made foundational dynamic-oligopoly and estimation contributions. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin made important related contributions but would be additional to a three-person cap. Including them would dilute a very clear core.
assessment.maturity: The BLP papers date from the mid-1990s, with decades of confirmation across industries, and the tools are now standard. The field's earlier recognition is mostly through general prize categories, so the timing is ripe.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to include Bresnahan, whose earlier identification-of-conduct work is also seminal.
Whether the structural-IO contribution is seen as methodological rather than as a discovery about economies.
I work in a neighbouring field (IO and trade), which could bias my familiarity upward; I treat this as a disclosure, not a merit signal.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The alternating-offers bargaining model with a unique subgame-perfect equilibrium is a foundation of non-cooperative game theory. It underlies models of wage setting, trade and decentralized markets, and the Rubinstein-Wolinsky market-bargaining work extended it to search and matching.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein is clearly central (1982). Wolinsky is credited for market bargaining and for work with Rubinstein and Binmore. Binmore's contributions (the Binmore-Rubinstein-Wolinsky link to Nash bargaining) are real but secondary to the core result, and Stahl's parallel contribution is not listed.
assessment.maturity: More than forty years of confirmation and deep integration into textbooks and applied theory. The main risk is delay rather than lack of evidence.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees bargaining as sufficiently distinct from earlier game-theory prizes (Nash, Harsanyi, Selten, Aumann, Schelling, Myerson, Maskin and Hurwicz, Milgrom and Wilson).
The right set of co-recipients, with Binmore and Wolinsky as the main alternatives.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression moved empirical analysis beyond conditional means to the whole distribution. It is used extensively in labour, inequality, finance and risk work, and it is robust and interpretable.
assessment.attribution: The original Koenker-Bassett (1978) paper is the clear anchor, and Koenker's later theory and software built the field. Chernozhukov contributed important later extensions (instrumental and inference theory), but his work is more naturally credited under other themes.
assessment.maturity: Close to five decades of use, with strong confirmation and widespread adoption. The econometrics prizes of 2021 (Angrist and Imbens) and earlier (Heckman and McFadden, Engle and Granger) set precedents for methodological recognition.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views quantile regression as a statistical-method contribution that is more naturally credited to statistics.
Whether Bassett's role is judged as large as Koenker's.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting reshaped trade theory after the 'new trade theory'. The framework explains within-industry reallocation, the intensive and extensive margins, and a new channel for gains from trade, and it is the workhorse of modern empirical trade.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution, building on Hopenhayn-style heterogeneity. Helpman's wide-ranging role (with Melitz and Yeaple on exports versus FDI, and earlier new trade theory) is substantial. Redding's quantitative and spatial extensions are important but later, and Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, who made parallel empirical and theoretical contributions, are not credited on this ballot.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation, although some quantitative welfare claims are debated. Krugman's 2008 prize recognised the earlier new trade theory.
uncertainties: Credit is contested among Melitz, Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum and Helpman.
The size of the welfare gains from selection varies by specification.
I am close to this field and have an affinity with its topics; that is not evidence of merit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data showed how mobility varies across places and cohorts and identified causal neighbourhood effects, with large influence on public policy and on public economics and labour practice.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is central and Hendren is the key co-author on causal place effects. Friedman and Katz contributed substantively, and the team-based nature of the work complicates a three-person cap.
assessment.maturity: The work is largely from the 2010s and 2020s. Replication and external validity are still being tested, and the prize would be early relative to the typical lag.
uncertainties: Long-run confirmation of the causal neighbourhood estimates.
How the team structure, including the Opportunity Insights collaborations, should translate into credited names.
The relatively short time since the main results.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The HANK framework (Kaplan-Moll-Violante 2018) showed that household heterogeneity in liquidity matters for monetary transmission, changing how macroeconomists think about policy channels and marginal propensities to consume.
assessment.attribution: The three credited names are the core of the HANK contribution. It builds on earlier incomplete-markets models (Aiyagari, Bewley, Huggett, Krusell-Smith), whose originators are not credited here, which weakens attribution.
assessment.maturity: A decade old, with rapid adoption but limited track record. Some findings are still contested.
uncertainties: Whether central results are robust to alternative calibrations and to empirical evidence on transmission.
The relation to the earlier incomplete-markets literature and the priority of those authors.
Whether the contribution is yet mature enough for a prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology (building on Autor-Levy-Murnane) and the China-shock evidence showed that trade and technology reshape local labour markets with persistent adjustment costs. The work influenced policy debates across trade and labour economics.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both strands. Hanson and Dorn are key for the trade-shock work, and the task framework also owes much to Acemoglu and Restrepo and others who are not listed. Katz is credited on a different ballot and is not proposed here.
assessment.maturity: The China-shock results date from the 2010s. Longer-run evidence is still accumulating, and some interpretations (the size of the effects and their mechanisms) are debated.
uncertainties: Whether the identification strategy (shift-share instruments) withstands current scrutiny.
Overlap with the 2024 and 2025 prizes on technology and growth, and with the Acemoglu-related task literature.
The relatively short time since the main findings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) showed how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks, a central mechanism in explaining credit cycles and financial crises. It remains foundational for macro-finance and policy models.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clear authors of the core model. The financial accelerator (Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist) is closely related, but Bernanke's 2022 prize partly recognised that line of work, and Gertler and Gilchrist are better treated as a separate contribution.
assessment.maturity: Close to three decades of influence and heavy use after 2008. Strong theoretical standing, though empirical quantification is mixed.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on banking and financial crises and with Bernanke's accelerator work.
Whether the committee prefers to credit the accelerator trio instead.
